description: SECTOR 17 is a student-led team competing in the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge in Thrissur, Kerala. We aim to build an engaging Space Mission Design Game combining software development, game design, and scientific problem-solving. We welcome motivated teammates interested in coding, game development, physics, astronomy, UI/UX, and data visualization. We value creativity, collaboration, and learning by building.
summary:
SECTOR 17 — THE LAST EXPEDITION is a browser-based Space Mission Design Game that puts players in command of EXPEDITION-V, a fictional mission to Jupiter’s icy moon Europa. Players select mission objectives, configure the AETHON spacecraft, balance propulsion, power, mass and thermal constraints, plan orbital manoeuvres, operate the spacecraft, communicate across deep space and process simulated scientific observations.

The game uses real aerospace concepts and equations, including the Tsiolkovsky rocket equation, Vis-Viva orbital mechanics, Hohmann transfers, inverse-square solar irradiance, radiative thermal balance and deep-space communication models. Its guided campaign turns these interconnected engineering challenges into an interactive learning experience.

By combining 3D visualisation, a deterministic simulation runtime, mission decisions and a multi-stage science data pipeline, SECTOR 17 aims to make complex space exploration concepts more accessible, engaging and understandable.
details:
SECTOR 17 — THE LAST EXPEDITION is an interactive Space Mission Design Game built around EXPEDITION-V, a fictional robotic survey mission to Europa, Jupiter’s icy moon. The player takes the role of mission director and flight operations lead, making engineering and operational decisions throughout the expedition.

The experience follows six main stages: Main Menu, Mission Selection, Spacecraft Workshop, Trajectory Planner, Mission Operations and Mission Debrief. In the Workshop, players configure the fictional AETHON spacecraft by selecting propulsion, electrical power and scientific payload components while monitoring mass, power and thermal budgets. The Trajectory Planner introduces orbital transfer planning and manoeuvre decisions. Mission Operations presents spacecraft telemetry, communications and science-processing controls. The Debrief records mission outcomes and player decisions.

The simulation incorporates established aerospace concepts, including the Tsiolkovsky rocket equation, Vis-Viva equation, Hohmann transfers, inverse-square solar irradiance, Stefan–Boltzmann radiative balance, Friis transmission loss and Shannon channel capacity. Orbital mechanics uses a classical Keplerian two-body approximation, while the thermal subsystem uses a simplified single-node model. Science observations are simulated: the data pipeline demonstrates Level 0 ingestion, Level 1 calibration and Level 2 analysis, including illustrative candidate chemical matches and radar echo horizons. These are not real scientific discoveries.

The application was developed using React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Three.js and React Three Fiber. Its architecture includes a deterministic simulation runtime, an 18-stage campaign state machine, spacecraft subsystem models, browser-based persistence and Web Audio API sound effects.

The project aims to make the engineering trade-offs of deep-space exploration accessible through hands-on experimentation rather than passive reading. Players learn how mass, propulsion, power, thermal constraints, communication delays and scientific objectives interact in a complex mission.

The project was informed by NASA planetary imagery, Europa Clipper mission and instrument references, and Deep Space Network technical resources. AI tools assisted parts of software engineering, testing, technical writing and concept artwork; these contributions are disclosed in the project. The simulation logic and physics calculations execute as deterministic code.

Live project: https://sector-17.vercel.app
Source code: https://github.com/AadhilNandan/Sector-17
